channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [6] Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Y. Ikemoto, K. Sawada

Authors: N. Kida, T. Togashi, K. Tono, Y. Ikemoto, K. Sawada

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: New experimental technique using XFEL for ultrafast dynamics in solids, potentially relevant for CM.

Tags: #method #spectroscopy #ultrafast

Abstract: The authors show that hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses generate terahertz emission in ZnTe through X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG). The findings establish a route to probing second-order X-ray nonlinearity and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids.

item.title: [9] Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Edwin W. Huang, Daniel Jost

Authors: Eder G. Lomeli, Sarbajaya Kundu, Katarzyna Siewierska, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct RIXS measurement of electronic structure in a superconductor, highly relevant method interest.

Tags: #method #RIXS #electronicstructure #superconductor

Abstract: In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Here, the authors directly observe the corresponding Lindhard continuum in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
